comments.author: @wa1ser
comments.text:
🚫 Please Stop Teaching & Leading Sisters: The Canon Is Closed & The Creation Order Is Fixed.

To the lady "teachers" broadcasting on social media and those who support them: It is time to face the Word.

Many claim Jesus was just waiting for a "progressive" culture to let women lead, citing that He had things to say we "couldn't bear" yet (John 16:12).

The Holy Spirit came and gave us the Epistles to explain those very things. And what did the Spirit reveal? 1 Timothy 2:11-14 and 1 Corinthians 14:34-37.

If you cannot "bear" those verses today, it is not a timing problem; it is a heart problem. 📖⛔

The Chronological Reality:

Before you dismiss this as "old-fashioned" because Paul wrote 2,000 years ago, bear in mind that when Paul was writing and appealing to Creation, he was looking back 4,000 years. ⏳

He was not reacting to Roman culture; he was submitting to the Divine Order established at the beginning. 

If 4,000 years of history did not change the rule for Paul, 2,000 years of "progress" does not 
change it for you.

The Creation Root and The Curse:

Eve was deceived first. Adam was formed first. This is not "culture"; it is Creation Order.

Furthermore, the Curse in Genesis 3:16 warns that the woman’s "desire" would be for her husband (a desire to usurp his position), yet he was to rule over her. When you step into the pulpit or broadcast as a teacher, you are living out the Curse, not the Calling. 🍎

The "Monstrous" Disorder:

As John Knox argued, it is a monstrous thing for a mouth to be found on a ribcage. The woman was taken from the man's side to be his helper, not his head. Men are the head of women and Christ is the head of men (1 Corinthians 11:3). To switch these roles is to create a spiritual deformity that defies the natural and divine order. 🦴🗣️

The Prayer Standard:

The Holy Scriptures never show women leading groups of people in prayer, irrespective of gender. In 1 Timothy 2:8, Paul specifies that he desires "the men" (Greek: andras – specifically males) to pray everywhere.

There is no biblical precedent for women to lead corporate prayer or "prayer sharing" groups.

To lead a group in prayer is an act of spiritual leadership that the Word explicitly reserves for men. 🙏🚫

The Judgment of Usurpation:

Isaiah 3:12 warns that when children are oppressors and women rule over the people, those who lead them cause them to err and destroy the way of their paths. 

Female leadership is not a sign of spiritual "progress"; it is a biblical marker of a people under judgment. 📉

The Kerusso Standard:

In the entire New Testament, the Greek word for official heralding or proclaiming (kerusso) is never used in relation to a woman. You can "post," but you cannot herald and teach. 📢📜

The 75km Check:

If God intended to use women to direct men, Agabus would not have had to take the "sandal express" 75km to deliver a message to Paul.

Philip had four "prophetess" daughters right there in the house (Acts 21). Why did God not use them? Because He does not outsource His authority to those He has excluded from teaching or usurping authority over men. 👣

The Limited Curriculum:

Look at the only command for women teaching women in Titus 2:3-5. The curriculum is strictly domestic: to love their husbands, love their children, and be keepers at home. 🏡

Scripture never commends or prescribes women teaching other women in spiritual or doctrinal matters.

Furthermore, the Bible never commends or prescribes women teaching other people’s children, regardless of the gender of the children.

If your "teaching" moves beyond the domestic sphere, you have abandoned your post. 🧶

The Phoebe and Junia Myths:

Do not be deceived by titles. Phoebe was a servant (diakonos), not an officer. If the Holy Spirit intended to label her a "deaconess," He had a specific word available (diakonissa) that he chose not to use. 🛡️

Likewise, Junia was well known "to" the apostles, not one "of" the apostles. Being recognized by leadership is not the same as holding the office of leadership. 🔍

The Danger of Pragmatism:

Many argue that because a woman’s teaching is "good" or "true," it must be acceptable. Pragmatism is never without punishment.

Remember Moses: he smote the rock twice when he was told to speak to it. Water still poured from it. The "result" was there, but because he disobeyed the method, he was barred from the Promised Land. He had to die east of the Jordan River as a result.

A lady may write something true, but if she broadcasts it as a teacher she is smiting the Rock. God’s grace in providing water is not an endorsement of your rebellion. We should never sin so that grace may abound.

Exceptions Prove Rules:

Exceptions prove there are rules and norms, not the other way around. ⚖️

Mary Magdalene was a witness to a fact, not a teacher of doctrine. Priscilla accompanied her husband who gave a private correction, not a public broadcast. Deborah sang a great song and helped a man deal with an enemy in a tent. But none of these exceptions change the creation order or the rules for the church and all those who consider themselves spiritual. ✨

Concerning Callings:

Sisters, there is such a thing as a spiritual prank phone call. Let’s talk about these callings. ☎️ 😬 

The spirit isn’t calling you to something that the Word forbids (or at least the *Holy* Spirit isn’t). Always test the spirits with the Word. You may feel called to leading or teaching in a parachurch or parasocial ministry, but Jeremiah 17:9 reminds us that the heart is desperately wicked, deceitful above all things and unknowable.

We need to be Bereans in accordance with Acts 17:11 and compare everything we think we’re hearing (whether it’s a voice in our head, our hearts or something someone says) with the Holy Scriptures.

The Bottom Line:

Broadcasting "teaching" is a direct violation of the order established from the beginning. Stay in the lines God drew. It is not a suggestion; it is the Commandment of the Lord. Remember in Luke 19:27 the fate of all those who would not have the Lord Jesus Christ reign over them. 😵 

Grace and peace, Beloved. 💜
